source_evidence.observation: The input format has precision t, unit roundoff u, and normalized range bounded by f_min and f_max; the accumulation format has precision T >= t, unit roundoff U, and normalized range bounded by F_min and F_max. Equation (2.3) models input rounding under the assumption that overflow does not occur.
Accumulation operations are rounded in the accumulation format. Equations (2.3) and (2.4) use round-to-nearest by default; the paper states how their constants change for directed rounding.

source_evidence.anchor: section 3 opening, equation (3.1), and following scaling assumptions
source_evidence.observation: For A in R^(m x n) and B in R^(n x q), equation (3.1) applies nonsingular diagonal row and column scalings, rounds the scaled inputs, multiplies them, and applies the inverse scalings. The diagonal factors are powers of two, and outer storage/scaling underflow and overflow are excluded.

The paper says that the maximum coefficient of each scaled row and column lies in (theta/2, theta]. Preventing input overflow requires theta <= f_max, preventing accumulation overflow requires theta <= sqrt(F_max/n), and equation (3.2) selects theta = min(f_max, sqrt(F_max/n)).

For a row x and column y, the corresponding power-of-two factors satisfy theta/(2||x||_infinity) < lambda <= theta/||x||_infinity and theta/(2||y||_infinity) < mu <= theta/||y||_infinity. Equation (3.3) defines the inverse-scaled inner product of the rounded inputs.
The paper later distinguishes s from the accumulation-computed value s-hat, with s-hat = s + epsilon_2, and ultimately from the exact inner product x^T y.

binders: [Explicit] A in R^(m x n), B in R^(n x q), and C = AB, with n the shared inner dimension. (PDF p. 4, printed B788, section 3 opening before equation (3.1).)
[Explicit] Lambda and M are nonsingular diagonal matrices with diagonal coefficients lambda_i and mu_i. (PDF p. 4, printed B788, prose following equation (3.1).)
[Explicit] theta is the permitted maximum scale for entries of Lambda A and BM. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, paragraph preceding equation (3.2).)
[Explicit] x is a row of A, y is a column of B, and lambda and mu are their corresponding scaling factors. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, section 3.1 and equations (3.3)-(3.4b).)
hypotheses: [Inherited] The product is evaluated using the mixed-precision MMA unit of Model 1, with an input format and an accumulation format. (PDF p. 2, printed B786, Model 1; PDF p. 4, printed B788, section 3 opening.)
[Explicit] Lambda and M are nonsingular and diagonal. (PDF p. 4, printed B788, prose following equation (3.1).)
[Explicit] Every lambda_i and mu_i is a power of two so that scaling introduces no rounding error. (PDF p. 4, printed B788, prose following equation (3.1).)

[Explicit] Underflow and overflow are absent before multiplication by Lambda and M and after multiplication by Lambda^(-1) and M^(-1); A, B, and C are stored in sufficiently high precision to be represented exactly. (PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, paragraph spanning the page break after equation (3.1).)
[Explicit] theta is selected as min(f_max, sqrt(F_max/n)). (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equation (3.2).)

[Unstated well-definedness requirement] n must be positive, and equations (3.4a)-(3.4b) require ||x||_infinity and ||y||_infinity to be nonzero. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equations (3.2), (3.4a), and (3.4b).)
conclusions: [Explicit] The scaling recipe is C = Lambda^(-1)(fl(Lambda A) fl(BM))M^(-1). (PDF p. 4, printed B788, equation (3.1).)
[Explicit] The selected range threshold is theta = min(f_max, sqrt(F_max/n)); the square root covers F_max/n. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equation (3.2).)

[Explicit] The paper states that the maximum coefficient on every row of Lambda A and every column of BM lies in the half-open interval (theta/2, theta]. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, maximum-coefficient paragraph preceding equation (3.2).)
[Explicit, row part] For a row x, its power-of-two factor lambda satisfies theta/(2||x||_infinity) < lambda <= theta/||x||_infinity. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equation (3.4a).)
[Explicit, column part] For a column y, its power-of-two factor mu satisfies theta/(2||y||_infinity) < mu <= theta/||y||_infinity. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equation (3.4b).)

[Algebraic consequence for nonzero x and y] Since powers of two are positive, equations (3.4a)-(3.4b) give theta/2 < lambda||x||_infinity <= theta and theta/2 < mu||y||_infinity <= theta. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equations (3.4a)-(3.4b).)
definitions_and_conventions: [Explicit] The input-format maximum normalized value is f_max = 2^(e_max)(2 - 2u), and the accumulation-format analogue is F_max = 2^(E_max)(2 - 2U). (PDF p. 2, printed B786, Model 1.)
[Explicit] fl denotes rounding to the input format. (PDF pp. 3-4, printed B787-B788, explanation after equation (2.3) and prose following equation (3.1).)

[Inferred from conformability] Lambda is m x m and scales rows of A, while M is q x q and scales columns of B. (PDF p. 4, printed B788, equation (3.1); PDF p. 5, printed B789, maximum-coefficient paragraph.)
[Conventional reading] ||x||_infinity and ||y||_infinity are vector infinity norms, hence maxima of absolute component magnitudes. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equations (3.4a)-(3.4b).)
implicit_context: [Inherited] n is both the column count of A, the row count of B, and the length of each row-column inner product. (PDF p. 4, printed B788, matrix dimensions; PDF p. 5, printed B789, section 3.1.)

[Inferred] Each lambda_i is selected for one row of A and each mu_j for one column of B before assembling Lambda and M. (PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, equation (3.1), maximum-coefficient prose, and equations (3.4a)-(3.4b).)

[Explicit rationale] Increasing theta reduces underflow, so the paper chooses the largest theta satisfying both stated overflow restrictions. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, paragraph preceding equation (3.2).)

[Unstated domain restriction] The row and column interval claims are meaningful as written only for nonzero rows and columns. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, maximum-coefficient prose and equations (3.4a)-(3.4b).)
statement.algorithm_linkage: Equation (3.1) is the scaled mixed-precision MMA recipe: diagonally scale A and B, round Lambda A and BM to the input format, form their matrix product using the Model 1 setting, and undo the diagonal scalings. For one row-column pair, equation (3.3) calls the exact inverse-scaled inner product of the rounded inputs s; the accumulation-computed value is introduced separately as s-hat in equation (3.17). (PDF p. 4, printed B788, section 3 opening and equation (3.1); PDF p. 5, printed B789, equation (3.3); PDF p. 6, printed B790, equation (3.17).)
numerical_model: [Inherited] The input format has t bits, unit roundoff u = 2^(-t), and maximum normalized value f_max; the accumulation format has T >= t bits, unit roundoff U = 2^(-T), and maximum normalized value F_max. (PDF p. 2, printed B786, Model 1.)
[Inherited] Assuming no overflow, input rounding obeys fl(z) = z(1 + delta) + eta with |delta| <= u, |eta| <= g_min, and eta*delta = 0. (PDF p. 2, printed B786, equation (2.3).)
[Inherited] Accumulation operations use the analogous accumulation-format model with U and G_min. (PDF p. 3, printed B787, equation (2.4).)

[Inherited] The default model is round-to-nearest; directed rounding is covered only after doubling the corresponding roundoff and underflow constants. (PDF p. 3, printed B787, paragraph following equation (2.4).)
[Explicit] theta <= f_max prevents input overflow, while theta <= sqrt(F_max/n) is the stated accumulation-overflow condition. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, paragraph preceding equation (3.2).)
error_notions: [Explicit] Power-of-two diagonal scaling is assumed not to introduce rounding error. (PDF p. 4, printed B788, prose following equation (3.1).)

[Explicit] Rounding and possible input underflow occur in fl(Lambda A) and fl(BM); the selected passage does not assert an error bound for them. (PDF p. 4, printed B788, equation (3.1) referring to model (2.3); PDF p. 5, printed B789, equations (3.5)-(3.6).)

[Explicit distinction] s is the exact inverse-scaled inner product of the already rounded inputs, whereas s-hat later denotes the result including accumulation errors. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equation (3.3); PDF p. 6, printed B790, equations (3.17)-(3.20).)

[Scope] Equations (3.1)-(3.4) state a scaling and range contract, not a forward-error, backward-error, relative-error, or normwise-error bound. (PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, equations (3.1)-(3.4).)
norms: [Explicit] The scaling-factor bounds use the vector infinity norms ||x||_infinity and ||y||_infinity. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equations (3.4a)-(3.4b).)

[Inferred operational meaning] Multiplying those norms by the positive factors lambda and mu controls the maximum absolute entries of the scaled row and column. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, maximum-coefficient paragraph and equations (3.4a)-(3.4b).)
[Scope] No matrix norm or error norm occurs in the selected equations (3.1)-(3.4). (PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, equations (3.1)-(3.4).)
constants_and_indexing: [Exact constant] theta = min(f_max, sqrt(F_max/n)); neither the square root nor division by n may be dropped or moved. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equation (3.2).)

[Exact endpoints] The lower scale bound is strict and contains the factor 2, while the upper bound is non-strict: theta/(2||x||_infinity) < lambda <= theta/||x||_infinity, with the analogous formula for mu and y. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equations (3.4a)-(3.4b).)

[Index role] lambda_i scales row i of A and mu_j scales column j of B; the paper writes diagonal coefficients lambda_i and mu_i but does not spell out their index ranges. (PDF p. 4, printed B788, prose after equation (3.1); PDF p. 5, printed B789, row/column prose.)
[Dimension role] n is the common inner dimension and appears inside sqrt(F_max/n). (PDF p. 4, printed B788, dimensions of A and B; PDF p. 5, printed B789, equation (3.2).)
higher_order_terms: [None] Equations (3.1)-(3.4) are stated as exact identities, definitions, and inequalities; they contain no big-O term, asymptotic qualifier, or instruction to discard higher-order terms. (PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, equations (3.1)-(3.4).)
exceptional_values: [Explicit] The floating-point model used by fl assumes that overflow does not occur. (PDF p. 2, printed B786, text immediately before equation (2.3).)
[Explicit] The outer high-precision storage and scaling stages are assumed free of underflow and overflow. (PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, paragraph spanning the page break after equation (3.1).)
[Explicit] theta is selected to prevent overflow in the input and intermediate accumulation computations. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, paragraph preceding equation (3.2).)

[Not excluded] Underflow during conversion to the input format or during accumulation remains possible; increasing theta is said to minimize rather than eliminate it. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, paragraph preceding equation (3.2) and equations (3.5)-(3.6); PDF p. 6, printed B790, equations (3.16)-(3.18).)

[Unspecified] The selected passage gives no separate NaN, infinity, signed-zero, or saturation convention; A and B are introduced as real matrices. (PDF p. 4, printed B788, section 3 opening; PDF pp. 4-5, equations (3.1)-(3.4).)

[Unaddressed] Zero rows and zero columns make the stated interval and divisions in equations (3.4a)-(3.4b) impossible or undefined. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, maximum-coefficient prose and equations (3.4a)-(3.4b).)

undebatable_constraints: A faithful contract must retain theta = min(f_max, sqrt(F_max/n)) exactly, including the square root over F_max/n. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equation (3.2).)

The row factor must be a power of two and satisfy theta/(2||x||_infinity) < lambda <= theta/||x||_infinity, with strict lower and inclusive upper endpoints. (PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, power-of-two assumption and equation (3.4a).)
The adjacent column part must also be preserved: theta/(2||y||_infinity) < mu <= theta/||y||_infinity. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equation (3.4b).)

The source claims a scaled-row and scaled-column maximum in (theta/2, theta], operationally tied to infinity norms by equations (3.4a)-(3.4b). (PDF p. 5, printed B789, maximum-coefficient paragraph and equations (3.4a)-(3.4b).)

The diagonal scalings are nonsingular, use power-of-two coefficients, and are surrounded by an explicit high-precision no-underflow/no-overflow assumption. (PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, prose following equation (3.1).)

A universal formalization must explicitly handle or exclude zero rows and columns; the paper does not provide a zero-case convention. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, maximum-coefficient prose and equations (3.4a)-(3.4b).)
The input-rounded inner product s must not be conflated with the later accumulation-computed value s-hat. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equation (3.3); PDF p. 6, printed B790, equation (3.17).)

ambiguities.issue: Zero rows and columns are not addressed. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, maximum-coefficient paragraph and equations (3.4a)-(3.4b).)
ambiguities.evidence: For x = 0 or y = 0, the displayed denominators vanish, and the maximum absolute scaled coefficient is 0 rather than an element of (theta/2, theta]. The paper states no nonzero-row or nonzero-column hypothesis. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equations (3.4a)-(3.4b).)
ambiguities.impact: A formal statement must either assume the selected row or column is nonzero, restrict the range claim to nonzero rows and columns, or add a separately justified zero-case convention.

ambiguities.issue: The prose says "maximum coefficient" rather than explicitly "maximum absolute coefficient." (PDF p. 5, printed B789, paragraph preceding equation (3.2).)
ambiguities.evidence: Equations (3.4a)-(3.4b) use infinity norms, which control maximum absolute component magnitude, including for rows or columns containing negative entries. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equations (3.4a)-(3.4b).)
ambiguities.impact: The literal signed maximum and the maximum magnitude differ; the norm-based maximum-magnitude reading is strongly indicated but is not stated verbatim.

ambiguities.issue: The domain and representability of the power-of-two scaling factors are not specified. (PDF p. 4, printed B788, power-of-two assumption; PDF p. 5, printed B789, equations (3.4a)-(3.4b).)
ambiguities.evidence: The paper requires lambda_i and mu_i to be powers of two but gives no exponent range, storage format, or constructive selection rule for them. (PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, prose after equation (3.1) and equations (3.4a)-(3.4b).)
ambiguities.impact: Existence is immediate for unrestricted real powers 2^k with integer k and positive theta/norm ratio, but may require extra range assumptions if the factors themselves must belong to a bounded machine format.

ambiguities.issue: Equation (3.1) writes the scaled expression using C even though later pages distinguish the computed result from AB. (PDF p. 4, printed B788, equation (3.1); PDF p. 6, printed B790, equations (3.17)-(3.22).)
ambiguities.evidence: Section 3 first defines C = AB and then says "We compute" C by equation (3.1), while the later analysis denotes the accumulation-computed scalar and matrix by s-hat and C-hat. (PDF p. 4, printed B788, section 3 opening and equation (3.1); PDF p. 6, printed B790, equations (3.17) and (3.22).)
ambiguities.impact: Equation (3.1) should be treated as the algorithmic recipe, not as a claim that finite-precision evaluation is exactly equal to AB.

ambiguities.issue: The positivity assumptions needed by equation (3.2) are inherited rather than restated locally. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equation (3.2).)
ambiguities.evidence: Model 1 defines f_max and F_max as positive format maxima, but section 3 does not explicitly state n > 0 before using sqrt(F_max/n). (PDF p. 2, printed B786, Model 1; PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, dimensions and equation (3.2).)
ambiguities.impact: A self-contained formalization must include positive format maxima and a positive inner dimension.

contract_plain_english: Given real matrices A and B and the mixed-precision MMA model, scale each nonzero row of A and each nonzero column of B by a positive power of two, round the scaled inputs, multiply them, and undo the scaling as in equation (3.1). (PDF pp. 4-5, printed B788-B789, equation (3.1) and its surrounding assumptions.) Set theta exactly to min(f_max, sqrt(F_max/n)); this is the paper's largest threshold satisfying its input- and accumulation-overflow restrictions. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, paragraph before and equation (3.2).) For a row x, choose lambda with theta/(2||x||_infinity) < lambda <= theta/||x||_infinity, and analogously choose mu for a column y; consequently their scaled infinity norms lie in (theta/2, theta]. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, maximum-coefficient prose and equations (3.4a)-(3.4b).) The source does not define a valid version of these claims for zero rows or columns, does not specify a finite storage range for the power-of-two factors, and distinguishes the exact inner product of rounded inputs from the later accumulation-computed value. (PDF p. 5, printed B789, equations (3.3)-(3.4b); PDF p. 6, printed B790, equation (3.17).)
